correctness.rationale: Equal-parity pairs are identical or complements and never change. An unlike-parity pair agrees on one issue and differs on one. Away from weight ties it has exactly one update-causing issue, the differing issue for copying and the agreeing issue for opposition, so it independently converts the focal parity to that of the target with probability 1/2. Thus the entire parity dynamics is a lazy voter step, with probabilities i(N−i)/(2N²) each way and the other attempts retained as holding probability. With distinct agents the denominator is 2N(N−1). Endpoints are exactly the union of consensus and complementary-pair configurations; each interior state has a positive-probability path to an endpoint, implying finite mean absorption for fixed N. The bounded martingale fixes at N with probability a/N. Killing on endpoints gives Q^t 1 for survival. Taking first differences of the Poisson recurrence yields d_{i+1}−d_i=−2N(1/i+1/(N−i)); d_i=2N(H_{N−i}−H_{i−1}) telescopes and sums to zero across the N differences. Summation by parts gives the equivalent mean 2N[N H_N−a H_a−(N−a)H_(N−a)], yielding the claimed entropy limit from H_k=log k+γ+O(1/k) and an O(N²) maximum. The two-agent example has success probability 1/4 each attempted step, with copying giving consensus and opposition giving strict polarization; a similarity tie can instead freeze both parities. value.rationale: This motivates a structural invariant in the stochastic two-issue model rather than a new gambler's-ruin computation. Researchers comparing parameter-dependent convergence can know exactly when attraction versus opposition is invisible even to the full attempted-update absorption law, while still changing consensus versus polarization. The finite-N distribution and uniform polynomial mean bound rule out a plausible metastability mechanism in the stated regime.
